title: Python SDK: dataclass-driven checkpointed streaming protocol and idempotent retries
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a robust, ergonomic way for Python SDK users to consume long-running LLM responses as a stream while supporting: 1) safe retries with at-most-once or at-least-once guarantees, 2) compact, JSON-serializable checkpoints so clients can resume after transient failures, 3) first-class dataclass/Pydantic glue so structured outputs remain easy to validate and hydrate.

Goals: Provide a small API surface that: (a) defines a 'StreamCheckpoint' protocol implemented as lightweight dataclasses, (b) offers serializer helpers for checkpoint storage (JSON + optional compression), (c) integrates checkpointing into the existing streaming iterator API so resumes are transparent, (d) documents idempotency expectations and provides helper wrappers for common patterns (cursor-based resume, token-index resume, and event-sequence resume).

Non-goals: This ticket does not add cross-language SDK parity (TS/Go work tracked separately) and doesn't change server-side contract for streaming events beyond a stable 'sequence_id' and optional 'partial_output' fields that we already surface.
acceptance_criteria: API: Expose a StreamCheckpoint dataclass and Runtime helpers (serialize/deserialize) documented in SDK reference
Behavior: Consumers can persist a serialized checkpoint mid-stream and resume stream consumption from the same logical position after a transient 5xx or network failure
Safety: Retry wrapper ensures no duplicated user-visible structured events for the default idempotent resume mode; provide explicit opt-in for at-least-once semantics
Tests: Unit tests for serializer roundtrip, checkpoint-based resume logic, and integration test against a local streaming stub that simulates dropped connections
Docs: Code example in docs and short migration guide for existing iterator users
tasks: Design checkpoint dataclass fields and versioning strategy
Implement serializer/deserializer with backward compatible version header
Integrate checkpointing into StreamingIterator as optional checkpoint_hook
Add RetryWrapper to SDK that accepts a checkpoint provider and resume strategy
Write unit tests + integration test harness simulating network interruptions
Add docs + cookbooks with 2 examples (cursor-resume and token-index resume)
API review and cross-team review with runtime/servers to confirm sequence_id behavior
progress_updates: 2026-01-12: Initial design doc posted to internal drive (link below) describing three checkpoint formats: cursor, token-index, event-seq. Chosen to start with token-index + sequence_id as V1.
2026-01-19: Prototype dataclass and serializer implemented. Serializer prepends a small version header to allow future format changes. Verified roundtrip for simple token-index checkpoint.
2026-01-24: Hook added to StreamingIterator prototype. Iterator exposes 'save_checkpoint()' that returns a JSON blob. Resume API accepts that blob and seeks server-provided sequence position.

2026-01-28: Integration test harness added: local streaming stub that emits partial events and random disconnects. Verified resume works for ~95% of simulated disconnects; remaining failures due to server-side sequence gaps (tracked with servers team).

2026-02-01: Implemented RetryWrapper that wraps the user-supplied callable and uses checkpoint to retry until resume success or max attempts. Added exponential-backoff jitter. Edge cases: ephemeral side-channel outputs are marked non-idempotent in docs.

2026-02-03: API review meeting held. Feedback: make the dataclass field names explicit and avoid magic numeric indices; add an opaque 'metadata' dict in checkpoint for customer use. Adjusted API accordingly.
2026-02-05: Code submitted as draft PR; CI unit tests passing locally. Ready for eng review.
implementation_notes:
Chosen API:

- @dataclass class StreamCheckpointV1:
    model_name: str
    sequence_id: str  # server-provided monotonic id for events
    token_index: int  # offset in tokens within the current sequence/event
    metadata: dict = {}  # opaque JSON for callers

Serializer: base64(gzip(json.dumps({'v':1, 'payload': {...}}))). We encode to base64 to keep storage fields string-safe.

Resume semantics: SDK will call server streaming endpoint with 'resume_after=sequence_id' and 'start_token_index=token_index'. Server agreed to re-emit the current event from token_index onward. If server cannot satisfy resume (sequence gap), SDK surfaces a RetryError with cause 'sequence_gap' and includes the checkpoint back to the caller.

Idempotency model: default mode attempts to provide at-most-once semantics for 'structured' deserialized events by deduplicating events using sequence_id+event_local_index. For non-structured raw streaming (bytes), we provide helper to switch to 'at-least-once' mode and include user-facing docs about dedup handling.
risks_and_mitigations: Server sequence gaps: Mitigation — fallback to delivering best-effort partial output and mark resume failure so callers can re-run entire request (documented pattern)
Checkpoint format drift: Mitigation — version header and migration helpers in serializer; unit tests covering backward compatibility
Incorrect user assumptions about idempotency: Mitigation — clearly documented defaults, examples, and a 'safe_retry' helper that enforces dedupe based on sequence_id
testing_plan: Unit tests for StreamCheckpointV1 serializer/deserializer and invalid payloads
Integration test: streaming stub that simulates drop after N tokens and asserts resume returns identical structured items
Chaos test: randomized disconnects + server-side reorder simulation to assert proper error surfacing
Performance test: measure extra CPU overhead of checkpoint serialization on typical streaming workloads (<1% overhead target)
notes_for_reviewers: Look at the simple API shape first: is the 'token_index' field intuitive? Alternative was 'byte_offset' — we prefer token index for model-based resumes.
Confirm the serializer format is acceptable for our persistence backends (S3, Redis). Base64+gzip chosen to be storage-safe and compact.
Edge case: what is acceptable retry timeout budget for Dedicated customers? Suggest default max attempts=3 with exponential backoff (100ms -> 800ms). We can tune later.
Cross-team ask: runtime team to add server-side option to re-stream from token index for sequence_id resumes. Server PR linked above.
